chapter: Chicago years: recordings, Armstrong, wartime exit
title: Back home, New York with Lizzie Miles and Cliff Jackson, then Chicago
summary: He joined his sister Lizzie Miles in New York in 1926 with Cliff Jackson's band, broadcasting on WMCA for about eight months. He returned to New Orleans, then went to Chicago in 1929, and advises players to be themselves.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, where did you go to next?
Well, I came back to New Orleans.
Came back to New Orleans. Where did you play then?

Well, after that I went to New York in 1926. You were in New York. I played around New Orleans, went to New York. That's where I joined my sister, Lizzie Miles, international Creole song boy. She's known all over the world. So as I said before, it was Cliff Jackson's band. We used to broadcast over at WMCA nightly. We had a swell flow show there. I worked there for quite a while. After that job closed, I got homesick for the old New Orleans. So I could come back and play some more good jazz. I was just blowing and couldn't get used to those fellows the way they play. And they wanted you to play the way they want. And you can't play music that way. It's best to play the way you feel and the way you cut out to play. Whatever type of music you prefer, that's what you should stick at. Don't try to play like somebody else.
Well, did you ever play at any other time with your sister besides that New York engagement?

No, that was the only time because she had left here since I was a kid and she's traveled all over the world. She's internationally known. You worked with her approximately how long? Well, in New York? About eight months. About eight months. Yeah, about eight months.
Well, you came back to New Orleans in 1927. Yeah, came back. And you played here until about 1929.
